question: Which native Indian dynasty issued their own coins with portraits of their rulers on them?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Satavahana Dynasty **__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Satavahanas, also referred to as **the Andhras in the Puranas,** were an ancient Indian dynasty based in the Deccan region.
 
• **Simuka** was the founder of the Satavahana Dynasty. 
 
• The Satavahanas were the first native Indian kings to have issued** their own coins which had the rulers' portraits on them.**
 
• **Gautamiputra Satakarni** started this practice which he imbibed from the Western Satraps after vanquishing them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1d75d60574fe420cc9cd5e88dd7187040d6d9cfba781f583e94c680eaa7a720e.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rashtrakuta was **a royal Indian dynasty ruling large parts of the Indian subcontinent between the sixth and 10th century.**
 
• The earliest known Rashtrakuta inscription is a 7th-century copper plate grant detailing their rule from Manapura, a city in Central or West India.
 
• ​The foundation for the **Pandya supremacy** in south India was laid by **Maravarman Sundara I** early in the 13th century.
